name: Naga nationalism
summary: Naga nationalism holds that the Naga peoples of north-east India and north-west Myanmar are a distinct nation entitled to decide their own political future. Since the 1929 Naga Club memorandum it has demanded to be left free of outside rule, and the Naga National Council and later the NSCN pursued sovereignty by declaration, plebiscite and armed struggle. Its mainstream aims to unite Naga-inhabited areas (Nagalim), protect customary law, land and culture, and is strongly shaped by Christianity, while settlements such as Nagaland statehood and the 2015 framework show a coexisting accommodationist current.
scope: The mainstream Naga independence movement as documented for the Naga Club (1929), the Naga National Council under Phizo (1946 onward) and the NSCN (1980 onward, especially NSCN-IM under Muivah). It excludes the Heraka religious strand, which was hostile to Christian converts, and Indian-state Naga politicians who accept Nagaland statehood without sovereignty. Economic and social questions are mostly unaddressed in sources, so most such answers are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Angami Zapu Phizo
keyFigures.role: Led the Naga National Council toward secession and formed a government in exile in 1956.

keyFigures.name: Thuingaleng Muivah
keyFigures.role: Co-founder of the NSCN in 1980 and leader of its NSCN-IM faction.

keyFigures.name: Isak Chishi Swu
keyFigures.role: Co-founder of the NSCN in 1980 and chairman of NSCN-IM.

sources.author: Morung Express
sources.usedFor: Quoted fragments of the 1929 Naga Club memorandum (leave us alone to determine for ourselves) and its defence of customary law and land; the full text was not opened.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Naga nationalist sources document no health policy; the NSCN's socialist label suggests state provision, but this is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Naga nationalist sources never address wage law, and a largely agrarian, village-based society gives no clear signal.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The NSCN's socialist and Maoist-influenced self-description points away from laissez-faire, but its economic program is thinly documented.

public-ownership.rationale: The NSCN calls itself socialist, yet Naga land is held communally by villages and clans rather than by a state, so adherents are split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented position; the movement's concerns are sovereignty and identity, not progressive taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not a documented concern of the nationalist movement.

property-fundamental.rationale: The 1929 memorandum defends community land and customary law against outside taxation, so property is communal and not an absolute individual right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The sources do not discuss corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: No documented position on welfare programs.

worker-ownership.rationale: The NSCN's socialist label is not tied in the sources to worker-owned firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A movement that has fought a long insurgency against Indian security forces would be wary of state surveillance, though this is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Christian-influenced nationalism and the NSCN's own public stance on drugs (Indian Army alleges trafficking, which the group denies) suggest opposition; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: The NNC under Phizo and the NSCN under Muivah were leader-centred, but adherents also stress consensual village democracy.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement demands a sovereign state of its own (Nagalim), which is incompatible with seeing the state as unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: The movement took up arms and ran parallel armies, so strict gun limits sit badly with it; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: The movement's grievance is against Indian military power (e.g. the 1950s counterinsurgency), though it values its own armed wing.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Christian-majority Naga society makes this unlikely to be supported; inferred, not documented.

decide-locally.rationale: Before British rule each Naga village was effectively sovereign, and nationalists defend village and tribal self-governance.

rehabilitation.rationale: No documented position on penal policy.

traditional-family.rationale: The memorandum defends Naga customs, and Naga society is strongly Christian and customary, so traditional family values are likely favoured.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Christian-majority Naga society is socially conservative; no movement source addresses it directly.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the Baptist Christian majority; not documented for the movement.

more-religion-public.rationale: The NSCN proposed Christianity as the state religion and its slogan is Nagaland for Christ, though Muivah has also said the state should be secular.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The movement frames its grievance as ethnic and national subjugation, but racial-justice policy is not addressed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; a Christian customary society is unlikely to adopt this view.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The 1929 memorandum asks that Naga customary laws and way of life be protected from outside law, and Naga nationalism is defined partly by promoting Naga culture.

gradual-change.rationale: The NNC and NSCN pursued rapid change by declaring independence and taking up arms rather than waiting for institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The movement guards Naga homelands and identity; Article 371A-style restrictions on outside land buyers fit this, though it is not documented in the sources opened.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Phizo appealed abroad (government in exile) for recognition of Naga independence, which suggests openness to international bodies; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Naga nationalists put Naga self-determination first, though the statement is about a state putting itself ahead of global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; the movement sought outside support for its own cause but took no stated view on intervention elsewhere.

open-borders.rationale: The movement seeks a bounded homeland, though it also wants to unite Nagas across the India-Myanmar border, so it opposes borders dividing Nagas more than borders in general.

limit-growth.rationale: No documented position on environmental growth limits.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources document no Naga view on technological progress, and the movement's concerns are political status and identity.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No Naga nationalist source discusses nuclear power, and there is no basis to infer a side.

revolution-justified.rationale: The NNC and NSCN made armed insurrection against Indian rule a central method, and the NSCN formed in 1980 expressly to continue it.

experts-over-public.rationale: Naga political tradition rests on village elders and consensus, which fits rule by the community, not experts; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: The NSCN is described as socialist but its economic planning is not documented in the sources opened.

land-value-tax.rationale: Naga land is held customarily by clans and villages, and no source mentions a land tax; the 1929 memorandum objected only to outside taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Naga customary inheritance is clan-based and no source addresses inheritance tax, so no side can be inferred.

basic-income.rationale: The movement's sources never discuss income guarantees, and a stateless insurgent movement has set out no welfare design.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses tariffs; Nagaland has little industry and the movement frames its case politically.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The NSCN's socialist leanings might suggest it, but nothing documents it.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Naga land tenure is communal by clan and village, which fits neither this statement nor its opposite cleanly.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Despite socialist branding, there is no sign the NSCN seeks to abolish money or wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed anywhere in the Naga nationalist sources.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The sources show no interest in state-recognised wage bodies; Naga organisation is by village, clan and tribe.

one-party-rule.rationale: The NSCN aims at a single Naga state under its leadership, but sources do not state a one-party doctrine; adherents are split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Pre-colonial Naga villages were ruled by elders and chiefs in a mostly egalitarian way, and the movement proposes no monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Village democracy and tribal consensus are valued, though modern nationalist organisations were often authoritarian.

direct-votes.rationale: The NNC held a 1951 plebiscite on independence, showing a taste for direct popular votes on the national question.

workers-councils.rationale: There is no documentation of council-based power; Naga political organisation rests on villages, tribes and elders.

right-to-secede.rationale: The NNC declared independence and held a 1951 plebiscite for secession; the right of Nagas to leave India is the core claim.

natural-rulers.rationale: Traditional Naga society is largely egalitarian within villages, with chiefs holding limited authority.

political-violence-never.rationale: The NSCN and NNC defended armed struggle for decades; adherents reject absolute pacifism.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed as doctrine, though warrior traditions are part of Naga heritage.

separate-church-state.rationale: The NSCN proposed Christianity as state religion, though Muivah has said the state would be secular, so adherents are split toward the church-state side.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The NSCN invokes Christianity, but the sources emphasise Naga customary law as the legal base rather than scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement demands a sovereign state with its own army, not private provision of defense.

military-superiority.rationale: The movement has no state to speak of; it seeks sufficient strength to resist India, which does not amount to superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement defines the Naga as a distinct people and wants a state uniting all Naga-inhabited areas, though several Naga tribes are recognised.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The NSCN has Maoist influence but is chiefly nationalist, so class struggle is not its main account of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The NSCN calls itself socialist but sources give no egalitarian programme, and customary Naga society is relatively egalitarian within villages without stated outcome goals.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The 1929 memorandum insists the Nagas keep their land and customary rule, and the movement claims authority over Naga ancestral homelands.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The memorandum stresses that the Nagas were never conquered but forcibly subjugated by the British, but no reparations claim is documented.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nagas stress their own distinct nationhood, not unity with other peoples on religious or civilizational grounds.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Naga communal norms and Christian ethics favour community over individual self-interest; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Naga customary life places community and village obligations first, though this is inferred from customary law.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources say nothing about nature's intrinsic value, though traditional Naga culture is tied to the land.

limit-population.rationale: Christian-majority Naga society and a small people seeking to hold their homeland make population control unlikely; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; the movement seeks its own development, not a rejection of industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No source links Naga nationalism to technological acceleration, and its stress on preserving customs points no clear way.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from social conservatism; not documented.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred; Naga politics stresses personal and customary authority.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is not discussed, and the movement's stance on state surveillance is only inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The memorandum asks to be left alone as in ancient times, but modern Naga nationalism also embraces Christianity and statehood.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement is defined by a fixed aim of Naga self-determination, but no source states a view on judging policy by results.

direct-action.rationale: The movement combined armed and political resistance and did not rely on Indian parliaments, but it also later negotiated.

means-match-ends.rationale: Adherents used armed struggle for national ends while also invoking Christian values, and sources state no position on means matching ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing in Naga nationalism suggests abandoning farming and modern life; the movement seeks a modern state.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Socialist labelling gives no specific doctrine.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The NSCN is Maoist-influenced but its sources do not state a theory of profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Despite Maoist influences the NSCN is a nationalist movement and does not describe a proletarian dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Land is held by clans and villages and farmed by households (jhum), not through collective state farms; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The NSCN has Maoist influences but the sources do not say it adopts the Leninist theory of imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: The NSCN itself collects taxes from the population; the memorandum objected to taxation by an alien ruler, not taxation as such.

harm-principle.rationale: No Naga nationalist source addresses the limits of state power over adults, and customary law is communal in outlook.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Naga nationalism claims rights for the Naga people as a collective and for customary community law.

conscription.rationale: The NSCN recruits for its armed wing, but there is no documented policy on conscription for a future state.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The sources never weigh exit against voting; the movement's own demand is to secede, which is a form of exit, but it also values popular votes.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from communal ethos.

positive-liberty.rationale: Naga nationalism is framed around freedom from alien rule and not around material preconditions of freedom, and nothing else is documented.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source discusses universities or media power, and the movement's grievance is directed at the Indian state.

organic-representation.rationale: Traditional Naga governance runs through villages, clans and tribal councils, which resembles representation by communities; inferred.

total-state.rationale: The NSCN's proposed state is not documented as totalising, and Naga village tradition is decentralised.

national-rebirth.rationale: Naga nationalists see the nation as already existing since ancient origins, and no source describes a decadence-and-rebirth narrative.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nagalim seeks to unite Naga-inhabited areas, a claim framed as self-determination rather than expansion into others' territory.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not documented; Naga villages were governed by elders and consensus.

bound-labor.rationale: Nothing in Naga nationalism supports serfdom; traditional village society was relatively egalitarian.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is not discussed in the movement's sources.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; Christian influence might favour it, but customary relativism pulls the other way.

single-common-good.rationale: The sources do not address whether politics seeks one common good; Naga consensus tradition and several rival factions both appear.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; some Naga Baptists identify with Israel, but no source documents a political stance.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No source addresses diaspora return, as the Naga claim concerns people already living on the contested homeland.

revive-national-language.rationale: Naga languages are numerous and English is Nagaland's official language; no revival policy is documented.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The sources do not discuss how companies are run, and Naga society has few large firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not discussed in the sources, and Nagaland's many mission schools make no side clear.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is outside what Naga nationalist sources address.

economic-freedom.rationale: No source links Naga political freedom to market freedom, and the NSCN's socialist label cuts against assuming it.

rule-by-example.rationale: The sources do not describe rule by moral example; Naga elders governed by custom and consensus, and the movement pursued laws and arms.

national-self-determination.rationale: Naga nationalism is defined as the ideology supporting self-determination of the Naga people, and the 1929 memorandum asked that Nagas decide their future.

force-without-un.rationale: The movement has no state or foreign policy to apply this to, and sources are silent on UN authorisation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The NSCN slogan Nagaland for Christ and Christian identity make faith central to the movement.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Immigrant welfare is not discussed by the movement, which is concerned with indigenous Naga rights.

class-collaboration.rationale: The NSCN's Maoist influences point one way and village egalitarianism the other.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement is organised around preserving inherited Naga culture and customs.

dominated-front.rationale: India alleges NSCN foreign ties with China, which is disputed; no stated doctrine of a common front.

workers-nation.rationale: Not applicable; the movement is nationalist and not organised along class lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Customary Naga law excludes women from inheritance and village councils, but sources do not document a movement stance on law.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest on loans is not discussed in the sources, and Baptist Christian Nagas do not generally prohibit it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The movement seeks self-rule for a people, not legal racial classification and segregation within a state.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Maoist influences might suggest it but the sources do not state it.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: No source addresses fossil fuels, though Naga nationalists have questioned who controls the resources under Naga land.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; the movement protects Naga distinctiveness but outside settlers are not discussed in the sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed; Naga institutions rest on village and tribal representation.

national-mission.rationale: The movement seeks self-determination for Nagas, not spreading its government elsewhere.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The movement's sources do not discuss patriarchy, and customary Naga law gives men the formal public roles.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The nationalists often portray Indian authorities as alien rulers, but no general claim about elites is documented.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: No sign of eugenics in Naga nationalism and Christian values oppose it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Nagas have long demanded accountability for Indian security-force abuses during the counterinsurgency, though the sources opened do not detail this.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement's stated aims are state-building with socialist leanings, not a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not documented as a movement position.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Christian ethics suggest equal moral worth, though customary law differentiates by gender; not documented.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The NSCN is a national movement, and its sources do not discuss socialism in one country or world revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The memorandum presents British rule as forced subjugation, and nationalists see Indian rule over Nagas as alien; the statement is about settler states, so low.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Naga nationalists defend Naga customary law against outside legal systems.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The movement is Christian-identified and values missionary heritage, so it would oppose restricting conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Nagas traditionally eat beef and are largely Christian, so adherents reject such a ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Christian identity is central, so strict secular schooling is likely opposed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Sources state no doctrine on the socialist state's withering away.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The memorandum and 1951 plebiscite rest the claim to independence on Naga consent and refusal to be governed by outsiders.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance is not discussed in the sources.

population-transfer.rationale: The movement wants to unite Nagas in one homeland but does not advocate expelling minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The movement has used armed force for its aims, so adherents do not treat initiating force as absolutely wrong.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement's sources do not state a Darwinian or competitive theory of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: India has banned NSCN factions, which the movement resents; inferred opposition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The memorandum's demand to be left alone and free of alien rule matches the idea of freedom as non-subjection.

separated-powers.rationale: No source describes the separation of powers in a proposed Naga state, so no side can be inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: The NSCN is Maoist-influenced but this doctrine is not documented.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The sources mention no priority for the poor, and the movement's concern is national status.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: This is a British housing policy with no Naga counterpart, and no source touches it.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is not discussed in the movement's sources.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The movement attributes Naga hardship to conflict with India, not to population growth, but sources do not discuss poverty's causes directly.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Sources do not discuss diversity and cohesion in general, though Naga nationalism itself unites many tribes.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Naga tradition selects leaders by lineage, age and consensus, not lottery; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Sources do not state a view on emergency powers, though the movement has itself suffered under India's emergency laws such as AFSPA.

party-controls-media.rationale: The movement's sources do not say how a Naga state would treat media.

party-commands-army.rationale: The NSCN's army (NSCN-IM armed wing) answers to the organisation, but sources do not state a doctrine.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not discussed in the movement's sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Sources do not discuss pay for representatives.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The NSCN's internal discipline is not described in the sources opened, and its factional splits suggest it is not uniform.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The 2015 framework reportedly concerned shared sovereignty with India, but the sources opened do not describe it.

head-commands-forces.rationale: No source describes the command structure of a proposed Naga state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Naga Baptist churches are congregational, so bishop-governance would be foreign to them; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: The NSCN is led by a political and military leadership, and Muivah has said the state should be secular.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The sources do not apply a defeatist doctrine; Nagas in the British labour corps served in the First World War and then formed the Naga Club.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship of art is not discussed in the sources, though conservative Christian norms might favour it.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits for presidents are not addressed in the movement's sources.

recall-officials.rationale: The sources do not discuss recall of officials.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The sources describe no alliance policy for a future Naga state.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed in the sources, and Naga land is owned customarily by clans and villages.

people-in-arms.rationale: The movement has relied on armed volunteers, but no doctrine of replacing a professional army is documented.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources do not praise rural over urban life, though most Nagas live in villages.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The NSCN aims at Nagalim, uniting Naga-inhabited areas across India and Myanmar into one state.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement's leaders were often educated elites, as the NNC's early leaders were, so it does not take this line.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The memorandum asks that Naga ways be respected on their own terms; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Sources do not state the movement's view on capital punishment.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: No source covers the teaching of creationism, though Baptist influence could favour it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The nation is defined as a people with common origin; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Naga languages are many and distinct; support for them is inferred, not documented.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The movement itself seeks protection for the customs and Christian practice of Nagas under Article 371A-type safeguards, but sources do not discuss exemptions as such.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Customary communal life favours conformity; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Foreign debt is not discussed by the movement.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Socialist NSCN may agree, but no source states it.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The sources do not describe how a Naga constitution would be written.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The sources link no political restrictions to development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Sources contain no position on global aid duties.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not applicable to a stateless movement.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources set out no form of head of state for Nagalim.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is not a Naga nationalist topic.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The NSCN has negotiated with India, but insists on Nagalim; not clear how it treats land-for-peace.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Naga customary land is held communally under village control, which fits property subordinate to the community.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The NSCN's Maoist influences point at most to some view of the Soviet Union, but no source states it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation philosophy is not discussed in the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: No source addresses alliance obligations, as the movement is a stateless one without treaty partners.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Nagas hold that India annexed Naga territory against the 1951 plebiscite result and treat Indian rule as unconsented.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Christian identity is central to the movement, so curbing churches would be opposed; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not discuss the role of a head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: India used police and army action against Naga independence from 1953, and nationalists reject that.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nagaland retains autonomy within India, and the 2015 framework concerned a special arrangement; the NNC first sought autonomy within India, so many adherents accept this.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Naga political tradition has no sacred ruler; village authority was by elders.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not discussed in the sources.

character-from-environment.rationale: The sources do not engage the nature versus nurture question.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Naga governance by customary law binds chiefs; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is outside the concerns of the movement's sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not discussed; Naga tradition mixes elders and village assemblies, but this is not stated as a doctrine.

leader-cult.rationale: Phizo and Muivah are widely honoured as leaders, but no source states a leader cult doctrine.

equal-parenting.rationale: Child custody law is not a topic in the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The sources do not discuss Maoist continuing-revolution doctrine, even though the NSCN has Maoist influences.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land is customary and held by villages and clans, with no landed estates to redistribute; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from stress on homeland.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Nagalim is a claim to neighbouring-state territory because Nagas live there, and the NSCN pursues exactly this.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not documented; the movement defends Christian conversion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Naga Christian culture has no such custom and nothing suggests the movement would require it.

common-currency.rationale: The movement has no stated monetary policy for Nagalim.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Nagalim unites related Naga tribes across the India-Myanmar border, and the Naga share an origin tradition at Mahkel.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Nagas want a state of their own, not merely cultural autonomy within a state, though the NNC first sought autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Naga nationalists want a homeland where they already live, but reject being merely a minority fighting for equal rights in India.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The NSCN has Maoist influences but its sources do not state this doctrine.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed in the sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The sources describe no relation between courts and majorities in a Naga state.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Customary Naga bodies have excluded women, and the movement has not pushed parity; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is not a documented Naga nationalist aim.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement standards are not discussed in the sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: The NSCN socialist and Maoist label might suggest it but nothing documents it.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The NSCN formed as an armed group to continue the independence struggle, though its stated aim is national, not social, revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Naga clan and chief traditions vary; no stated position.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Naga nationalism promotes Naga culture and a common origin story, which supports teaching history from the Naga standpoint.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The memorandum rejected alien British rule over Nagas, who said they had never been conquered.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism promoting Naga culture and flag (the NNC adopted a flag in 1956) suggests it; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; Nagas benefit from Scheduled Tribe protections in India.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources show no Marxist crisis theory, though the NSCN has socialist labelling.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The movement rejected outside imperial rule and holds no empire of its own.

delink-world-market.rationale: The sources state no development strategy for Nagalim.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The sources do not use Marxist labor-aristocracy analysis, even with the NSCN's Maoist influences.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from communal ethics; not documented.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: No source discusses a bill of rights for a Naga state, though Article 371A shows Nagas valuing entrenched protections.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The memorandum says the Nagas were never conquered and wanted to be left out of arrangements made without them, so imposed settlements bind no one.

elective-rulers.rationale: Naga villages chose leaders by custom and not birth in many tribes; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Naga traditional decision-making is by village consensus; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Nationalists resisted Indian authorities as lacking legitimacy, which is related but not the same claim.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Nagas have no monarchy to contest parliament, and the sources set out no constitutional design.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not discussed; traditional Naga culture includes hunting and eating many animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal welfare law is not discussed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Traditional Naga chiefs and elders had duties to the village, but the sources do not describe this as a doctrine of noble duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Adherents are political activists and fighters, and the movement is built on political engagement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-school cultural critique is not part of Naga nationalism.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is absent from the sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not stated in the sources, though NSCN-IM has Maoist influences.

native-born-offices.rationale: Defence of Naga self-rule and customary protections implies Nagas hold the offices; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: The sources do not discuss relations between communist parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Nagaland depends on central funds; no stated doctrine.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Nagalim claims Naga-inhabited areas but not as lost in a war.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The movement holds that Nagas as the indigenous people should govern Naga lands; there are no settlers in the usual sense.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The movement's sources do not discuss antifascism as a constitutional value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The sources do not take a position on equating fascism and communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is outside the movement's sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument politics is not addressed, though a movement defending heritage might favour preservation.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-attention policy is not discussed in the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not discussed in the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The memorandum asks that Naga customary law continue instead of foreign systems, which fits locally rooted institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The sources do not describe a guardian role for Naga armed forces in a future state.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care work pay is not a topic in the movement's sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from customary and Christian family norms.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service selection is not discussed; Naga tradition rests on lineage and village standing, not exams.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The sources show no policy on foreign takeovers.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Sources do not discuss imperative mandates, though village consensus tradition may be sympathetic.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pensions are not discussed in the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Naga land is owned by clans and villages in lasting customary tenure, not held only while used.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Budget powers are not discussed in the sources.

single-official-language.rationale: The Naga people speak many languages and the movement unites diverse tribes; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The memorandum opposes outside control of Naga land and Article 371A-type protections restrict outsiders, though not shown in sources opened.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The movement's sources do not discuss disparate-impact doctrine.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism is not discussed, though Christian and customary values might criticise it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The movement is a recipient, not a donor, of alleged foreign support, and it has no stated policy of arming others.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The movement rejects outside powers overriding a people's will.

corporate-influence.rationale: Corporate lobbying is not discussed in the sources.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; Naga churches rely on foreign mission links.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Family incentives are not discussed in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Naga customary land rules limit land to Nagas, which this fits; inferred from the memorandum's defence of land.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment guarantees are not discussed in the sources, though the NSCN has a socialist label.

democratic-peace.rationale: The movement's sources do not discuss democratic peace theory.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The movement rejects Indian law's authority over Nagas, but sources do not state a general claim that no duty to obey law exists.

non-intervention.rationale: The memorandum demands to be left alone and free from outside interference.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not documented as a movement theme.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Christian and customary marriage norms make abolition implausible.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The sources do not discuss freedom of information.

local-production.rationale: Local production is not discussed as policy, though Naga villages are largely agrarian and self-supplying.

informal-organisation.rationale: The NSCN is a formal party with an armed wing; the movement is not informal.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Nationalists appeal to international recognition while rejecting Indian jurisdiction; mixed.

religious-nation.rationale: The NSCN proposed Christianity as the state religion and the movement ties Naga identity to Christianity, though other strands such as Heraka differ.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The memorandum rejects subjection to outside powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The sources do not discuss fiscal sharing, although Nagaland depends on grants from the Indian centre.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The sources do not discuss the Marxist split of personal and productive property.

defeat-communism.rationale: The NSCN has Maoist influences and does not seek to defeat communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The sources show no policy on service delivery mix.

religion-illusion.rationale: The movement ties itself to Christianity (Nagaland for Christ), so it would reject the view that religion is a mere illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxist stage theory is not stated in the sources, even given Maoist influence on the NSCN.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The sources do not link women's equality to economic change.

socialized-care.rationale: Childcare provision is not a topic in the sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: English is widely used and the Naga languages are many; no purism is documented.

treaties-binding.rationale: The NNC sought honouring of the Nine-Point Agreement, which Indian Constituent Assembly refused to ratify.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Villages are self-governing and hold land communally, but the movement seeks a state.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The NSCN's name and socialist label suggest it does not reject socialism outright, and no source states a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The memorandum and Nagalim claim rest on Naga ancestral land and the Heraka pledge to reunite.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No part of the movement denies it, and Naga Christians are broadly aligned with Western sympathy for Israel.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; social attitudes are conservative but no stated law position.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The NNC and NSCN factions killed rivals, yet the movement officially claims popular legitimacy; split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Blasphemy law is not discussed, though the NSCN's Christian identity is documented.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The memorandum rejects imposed alien rule, and the movement opposes domination by outsiders.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is an Islamic doctrine with no Naga counterpart, and the sources do not discuss it.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The movement fights Indian rule on national grounds and not because India lacks religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Naga village decision-making is participatory by custom; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality is not discussed in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement defines itself by national self-determination, but sources do not discuss the left-right divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: The sources do not use the Marxist concept of alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Islam is not discussed in the Naga nationalist sources.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Christian identity of the NSCN suggests it, though not documented as doctrine.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace harassment law is not covered by the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: The sources do not describe a preferred economic order for Nagalim.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement maintains armed forces and seeks a state with its own army.

rich-first.rationale: The sources state no view on uneven development.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The sources do not state an alignment policy, and India alleges the NSCN has dealt with outside powers.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Not documented; inferred from non-hereditary tribal leadership.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit is not discussed in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The movement has no state to negotiate with lenders, and sources are silent.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement prizes popular self-determination and village consensus, and nothing supports property franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is not part of Naga nationalist sources.

reification.rationale: The Marxist concept is not used in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Press ownership is not discussed in the sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The memorandum defends established customary law as binding, which is close to rule by known standing laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement claims the vote for Nagas in their homeland but not exclusion by race as a doctrine.

online-participation.rationale: Online deliberation is not covered by the sources.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency tools are not discussed in the sources.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Naga society is overwhelmingly Christian, and sources do not discuss marriage law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: No source documents boycotts of minority-owned shops as a Naga nationalist tactic.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition is not discussed, though Naga village assemblies are a customary forum.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The sources do not discuss reform of Christian doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Wealth concentration is not discussed in the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The movement is Christian-identified and proposed Christianity as state religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The movement seeks a state with its own police and army.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Naga village and tribal consensus and the Nagalim plan for several tribes suggest sharing; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Naga churches and communities do charitable work, but the sources do not set charity against state programmes.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk is outside the sources' concerns.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Naga Baptist churches have been slow on women's ordination; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Customary Naga society is patriarchal; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The movement guards Naga self-rule; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Housing rents are not discussed in the sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not discussed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The NSCN has recruited youth but a drilled youth movement is not documented.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is not addressed in the sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The sources do not address foreign bases, though the movement opposes Indian military presence in Naga areas.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Nagas have called the counterinsurgency genocidal, but sources opened do not document it; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The NSCN's socialist label hints at the idea but sources state no income doctrine.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: A movement with armed wings defending Naga land does not hold that killing in self-defence is wrong.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Nagas hold a common origin at Mahkel and pre-colonial sovereign villages, which implies continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Sex and gender theory is not in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory debates are not covered by the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The NNC and NSCN honour fallen fighters as national martyrs, and the NNC treats Phizo's struggle as sacred, though sources opened do not detail rituals.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The NSCN slogan Nagaland for Christ casts the struggle in religious terms.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Nagalim aims to gather all Nagas in one state, not a cultural centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: The NNC and NSCN demanded a state and used arms; statehood came first.

god-not-male.rationale: Naga Baptist tradition uses conventional language, but the sources do not discuss it.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is not a topic in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Defence of Naga land and Article 371A-style protection suggests Nagas should control their economy; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: This is the Nagalim demand: merge Naga-inhabited districts of Assam, Manipur, Arunachal and Myanmar into one unit.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence is not discussed in the sources.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The NSCN is described as socialist, but sources do not state a workers-power criterion.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Water and local transport ownership are not discussed in the sources.

second-chamber.rationale: The constitutional design of Nagalim is not described in the sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Villages and clans hold Naga land communally, which resembles local-community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Naga villages were sovereign units; a federation of villages and tribes would suit the tradition, but it is inferred.

family-wage.rationale: The sources do not discuss wages, and household farming rather than wage labour dominates Naga economic life.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is outside the sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ageing research is outside the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Digital payments are not discussed in the sources.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity is not discussed in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: The sources frame rights collectively for the Naga people, and say nothing of persons as ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Christian identity of the movement implies a spiritual as well as material view of humans.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Nagas insisted on guarantees such as the Nine-Point Agreement and Article 371A, not powers India could withdraw.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetically engineered crops are not discussed in the sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban density is not a topic in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement organises around ethnic national interests rather than racial groups; not addressed in racial terms.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The movement frames its armed struggle as defence of Naga land, but it is stateless; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Naga identity rests on common origin, Christianity and customs, and the Naga speak many languages.

communal-electorates.rationale: The sources do not discuss separate electorates, though Nagas have asked for tribal customary representation.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Naga nationalists accuse India, not foreign powers, of dividing Naga lands, and sources do not state a partition-plot theory.

free-public-college.rationale: University tuition is not discussed in the sources.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is not discussed in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: The sources do not state a duty to future generations, though customary stewardship of ancestral land is plausible.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources do not discuss distinct values of women in public life.

arms-reduction.rationale: The movement keeps its armed wings and sources do not state an arms-reduction policy.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The sources do not discuss secret treaties, though the NSCN's talks with India have been held confidentially.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital flow policy is not discussed in the sources.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The NSCN maintains its own armed wings under ceasefire, and negotiations have not required complete disarmament.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The movement raises its own fighters and sources do not discuss refusal of orders.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The sources do not discuss wage bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits are not discussed in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not discussed in the sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The sources do not address the international economic order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Maoist influence suggests it but not documented.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The sources do not discuss economic pluralism among communities.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed in any source opened; the NSCN socialist label is too vague to infer price policy.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The movement defends community-held land under customary law, which sits poorly with pricing nature as capital; this is inferred from the 1929 memorandum on land.

sacred-nation.rationale: Naga nationalism ties the nation to shared ancestry, land and Christian identity that outlasts individuals, but sources do not use sacred language; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Naga nationalist sources never address student loans, and there is no basis for a lean.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The movement casts Indian rule as outside domination and Nagalim as a distinct nation, which fits a colonial framing of the centre-periphery relation, though regional exploitation is not documented.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The movement, strongly shaped by Christianity, likely accepts a common human nature grounding dignity; no source states it, so this is inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Naga nationalist sources never address broadcasting policy, and the movement has been in conflict with state authorities, so no lean is inferable.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Naga nationalism is strongly shaped by Christianity (NSCN: 'Nagaland for Christ'), whose exclusive truth claims sit badly with a view that all religions share one truth; inferred, not stated in the sources.

farm-price-support.rationale: Sources never address farm policy; Naga society is village-agrarian and the NSCN has a socialist label, but support for state price guarantees is not documented.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear weapons are irrelevant to a movement without a state; no position is documented and nothing in its principles settles it.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement is a national front across classes; its socialist label hints at class politics but no stance on workers' parties is documented.

ban-fgm.rationale: FGM is not practised among the Naga and sources are silent; Christian, rights-minded adherents would likely accept a ban, inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Naga customary law, which the movement defends (1929 memorandum), traditionally passes land through sons; a customary-law defender would resist changing this, inferred from s4.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The Naga tribes speak many distinct languages and the movement stresses tribal and Naga distinctiveness; inferred, as no source addresses naming of languages.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed by any source; no principle of the movement points to courts over agencies or the reverse.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The movement defends customary law and village institutions against outside rule (s4), so a formal advisory role for traditional leaders fits; the sources do not state this directly.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Sources do not address environmental policy; adherents' land attachment cuts both ways against restricting liberty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Criminal sentencing is not addressed in the sources; no clear inference from the movement's aims.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: A movement protecting a small nation's land and culture against outside settlement would plausibly expect newcomers to learn the local language; inferred from its defence of Naga distinctiveness.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Naga sources document no labour policy; the NSCN's socialist label and customary village structures give no clear lean on union dues.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; Naga nationalists have contested Indian elections as often as they have boycotted them.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the strongly Christian, Baptist-dominated character of the movement, which seeks Christian identity for Nagalim.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the movement stresses self-determination and customary consensus rather than a definition of democracy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the Christian, socially conservative character of mainstream Naga nationalism.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred: Naga areas have suffered Indian shutdowns under security laws, and the movement opposes outside coercive control; not stated in the sources.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; inferred from the NSCN's socialist label favouring collective provision over a cash-transfer scheme.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred: Naga women vote in Nagaland, but customary law bars them from village councils, so adherents are not united on equal office-holding.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the movement's strong Christian identity, which would reject the claim.

race-social-construct.rationale: Naga identity is framed as distinct nationhood by history and custom; the sources do not address race as a category.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from customary-law protection and the conservative stance on gender roles; no stated position on state agencies.

missingStatements.text: Customary law and land ownership of an indigenous people should be constitutionally protected from change by the national parliament without that people's consent.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1929 memorandum sought protection of Naga customary law and land from foreign law and taxation, and this is a defining concern of the movement.

notes: Most economic and social statements are not addressed by movement sources, so these are low-confidence inferences from Christian-majority customary society and the NSCN's socialist label. Muivah has said a Naga state would be secular while the NSCN has also proposed Christianity as state religion, so religion-and-state answers reflect a split.
